newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma again delays vote on oil reserve list.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma again delays vote on oil reserve list.

text.p: Conservative Russian deputies, dealing another blow to foreign energy investors, blocked on Wednesday a planned vote on a draft list of oil and other reserves open to production-sharing agreements.

The State Duma lower house of parliament was due to vote on the list at a special hearing on Thursday, but deputies, at the prodding of the ultra-nationalist Liberal Democratic Party, decided to postpone the vote until at least April.
The postponement was supported by 234 deputies and opposed by 127 members, with one parliamentarian abstaining from voting.

The reserves list, which itemises oil, gas and other fields open to development on a production-sharing basis, has undergone a major pruning to satisfy conservatives since it was first compiled last year.
The draft now contains around 20 or 30 fields, a fraction of the nearly 260 initially recommended by the government.
LDP leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky said that even the narrowed list would encourage separatism in resource-rich regions and deprive the budget of revenue.
The reserves list is an important cousin to the production sharing law, which was passed in 1995 but requires passage of both the list and certain amendments in order to function.

Around $60 billion in planned foreign oil investments hinge on the legislation. Foreign oil companies are worried that any reserves they might wish to tap and which are not on the list will require individual Duma approval.
This in turn would slow down or even jeopardise the investment process.
Conservatives have argued that the production sharing law and its sister legislation will award too many tax breaks to foreign companies and result in a cheap sell-off of Russian oil fields.
The original list accounted for 38 percent of Russia's total oil reserves.
